classification.difficultyReason: Uses exterior-angle equations with supplementary or vertically opposite angles.

content.prompt: Use the exterior angle theorem to find $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ or $\theta$ in the diagrams below.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with BC extended to D.
Thin triangle EXT with ETR straight; curved leaders identify X=20 degrees and E=24 degrees.
Right triangle ELG with NEL straight.
spec.mathematics: Exterior NEG=121 degrees, ELG=90 degrees; gamma=EGL.
Exterior RAE=70 degrees, AED=43 degrees; theta=ADE.

spec.description: Triangle AOT with BA TS horizontal, AOM vertical and WOT straight. Square marks BAO.
spec.mathematics: BAO=90 degrees and ATO=37 degrees; alpha=WOM.

answer.worked:
$\angle OAT=90^\circ$ (straight angle at $A$).

Exterior angle of $\triangle AOT$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle MOT&=90^\circ+37^\circ\\\angle MOT&=127^\circ\end{align*}$$
Straight angle at $O$:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+127^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=53^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle IEN with RIES, TINL and GNE straight.
spec.mathematics: RIT=71 degrees and GNL=81 degrees are vertically opposite interior angles; beta=SEN.

answer.worked:
$\angle EIN=71^\circ$ and $\angle INE=81^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles).

Exterior angle of $\triangle IEN$:
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=71^\circ+81^\circ\\\beta&=152^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle GTY above straight line EGYP.
spec.mathematics: Exterior angles EGT=157 degrees and TYP=140 degrees; gamma=GTY.

answer.worked:
Straight angle at $Y$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle GYT&=180^\circ-140^\circ\\\angle GYT&=40^\circ\end{align*}$$
Exterior angle of $\triangle GTY$:
$$\begin{align*}\gamma+40^\circ&=157^\circ\\\gamma&=117^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle KLC with JKLM straight and a curved leader into angle KCL.
spec.mathematics: Exterior JKC=77 degrees, KCL=20 degrees; theta=CLM.

answer.worked:
Exterior angle at $K$ of $\triangle KLC$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle KLC+20^\circ&=77^\circ\\\angle KLC&=57^\circ\end{align*}$$
Straight angle at $L$:
$$\begin{align*}\theta+57^\circ&=180^\circ\\\theta&=123^\circ\end{align*}$$
